chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Mufaddal ibn Yazid who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I forbid you from two characteristics in which lies the destruction of men. I forbid you from worshipping God through falsehood and from issuing fatwas to people about what you do not know.'

key_terms.بِمَا لَا تَعْلَمُ: About what you do not know — speaking on religious matters without established knowledge
key_terms.تَدِينَ اللَّهَ بِالْبَاطِلِ: To worship/make religion to God through falsehood — practicing religion based on false premises
key_terms.تُفْتِيَ: To issue fatwas — to give binding religious rulings
key_terms.خَصْلَتَيْنِ: Two characteristics/traits — referring to two dangerous spiritual-juristic vices
key_terms.هَلَاكُ الرِّجَالِ: Destruction of men — spiritual and moral ruin

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about issuing fatwas without knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) personally warned his companion Mufaddal ibn Yazid against two deadly spiritual traps: practicing religion based on falsehood and giving religious rulings without knowledge. This direct personal warning underscores that both religious innovation based on untruth and uninformed juristic opinion are paths leading to one's ruin. The original audience — scholars and students of religious law — would have understood that issuing fatwas without knowledge constitutes a grave sin and a misrepresentation of God's religion.
